title: Large-scale analysis of test-retest reliabilities of self-regulation measures
authors: A. Zeynep Enkavi, Ian W. Eisenberg, Patrick G. Bissett, Gina L. Mazza, David P. MacKinnon, Lisa A. Marsch, Russell A. Poldrack
venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences 116(12):5472-5477
caption_short: Schematic of a recent-probes trial (same task as the first session): six letters, a 3 s delay, then a probe letter to judge as in or not in the set.
notes: Drawn by us: none of the papers describing this dataset has a task figure for this task. Eisenberg et al. 2019 (Nat Commun, CC BY 4.0) has eight figures, all analysis figures (Fig. 1a only lists task names, including 'Adaptive N-back'); Enkavi et al. 2019 (PNAS) shows reliability results only; Eisenberg et al. 2018 (Behav Res Ther 101:46-57) lists the tasks in a table without figures; the Experiment Factory paper (Sochat et al. 2016, Front Psychol 7:610) shows software diagrams only. The task details in the schematic are taken from the task code that ran the study (github.com/expfactory/expfactory-experiments, MIT licence, recent_probes/experiment.js): 1 s red fixation, six letters in a 2 x 3 layout for 2.5 s, 3 s fixation, probe shown 2 s with a 7 s response window (left arrow = in the memory set, right arrow = not); each new set takes three letters of the previous set and three letters not used in the last two sets; probe types rec_pos / xrec_pos / rec_neg / xrec_neg in equal numbers (18 each over 3 runs of 24 test trials); 4 practice trials with feedback. The letters drawn are an example, not from a real trial. In the real task the letters are images of capital letters. Rendered with Pillow (DejaVu Sans). Same image as the recent-probes card; the retest used the same task.
